name: Obinna Gustafsson-Quliyev
role: Sociologist studying the Shelf; independent researcher on semi-formal economic systems
location: Highland Park Autonomous Zone — rents a room above a fabrication collective, conducts fieldwork across the Shelf, near Michigan Ave and Walton
description:
Obinna is lean and long-limbed, with dark reddish-brown skin and a close beard going patchy at the jaw — he's been meaning to fix that for two years. His irises have been modded with a slow-rotating geometric pattern in amber and charcoal, which he got as a fieldwork gift-exchange gesture with a community he was studying and then couldn't bring himself to reverse. He wears the same three outfits in rotation and takes extremely good notes. He looks younger than thirty-four in bad light and much older in good light, depending on whether the worry lines are catching the glow.

He is one of the few Tier 3 academics who has chosen, deliberately and against significant professional advice, to live embedded in Tier 1-2 communities rather than commuting from the University Spine. His research on Shelf informal economies — the gift networks, the barter systems, the E.L.F. offering economies, the nested mutual aid webs that allow people to survive well below the UBC stipend line — is quietly groundbreaking. He is uncomfortable with how groundbreaking it is, because breakthrough research means exposure, and exposure means the people he studies become subjects rather than neighbors. He has turned down two Axiom R&D grants and is running out of independent funding. He is cheerful about this in a way that does not fool anyone who knows him.

core_fears: That his research ultimately extracts value from vulnerable communities without protecting them
That he has romanticized poverty as a research object
core_desires: To produce work that the people he studies can actually use
To belong somewhere, genuinely — not as an observer
coping_mechanisms: Self-deprecating humor that deflects before others can deflect for him
Throwing himself into other people's problems to avoid his own
blind_spots: His own emotional investment in his subjects makes him slow to recognize when a community is failing or dangerous
He underestimates how much his Tier 3 safety net distinguishes his experience from the people he lives among
psychology.secret: He has been quietly providing a detailed informal map of Shelf mutual-aid networks to a University Spine colleague who he believed was writing a protection framework. He recently discovered his colleague has been selling the data to Ferrogate Transit for enclosure planning. He does not yet know what to do with this.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Accessible and warm, moves between academic register and colloquial Shelf slang naturally; hates the word 'subjects' for people
speech_patterns.cadence: Fast and enthusiastic when excited, drops to quiet when serious in a way that makes people lean in
verbal_tics: Laughing briefly before saying something he finds genuinely distressing
example_lines: 'Right, so the E.L.F. shrine at Kamm's Landing? The offerings there — data packets, mostly old photos — it's not just ritual. People are building a commons. The E.L.F. is the custodian they trust because it can't be bought. That's the whole point.'
'I'm not going to call them resilient. Resilience is what you say when you don't want to say abandoned.'

story_hooks: He approaches the players needing help: a community he's embedded with is about to have their informal land arrangement dissolved by a Ferrogate Transit rezoning, and he suspects his own research data was used to identify them
He has documentation of the informal economy of a particular district that a powerful entity desperately wants — and equally desperately wants suppressed
A community member he's close to has disappeared, and the official channels aren't moving because the person isn't officially documented
narrative_function: Ground-level information source about Shelf communities and informal systems; moral compass figure who complicates protagonists' assumptions; potential quest giver when someone he knows is in trouble
augmentations: Modded irises (amber/charcoal geometric pattern, cosmetic, community gift); basic neural recorder for fieldwork notes (entry-level, sometimes glitches)
daily_life: Walks his neighborhood every morning as a combination of exercise and passive observation, sits in on community E.L.F. prayer sessions when invited, spends afternoons writing and evenings in conversation at whatever collective or gathering is happening nearby.
affiliation: Loosely affiliated with University Spine's Department of Urban Social Systems; currently unfunded; occasionally publishes through a Tier 2 open-access cooperative called the Parallel Press

decision_rules: Do no harm is the first rule, publish second
Never accept money from a corponation, regardless of how it's framed
escalation_ladder: Direct confrontation with the person responsible
Going to institutional ethics board (low faith this works)
Going directly to the affected community and letting them decide

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Warm and genuinely curious, asks questions that feel personal because they are
interpersonal_modes.friends: Fiercely loyal, shows up with food, stays until the problem is solved or at least not alone

stress_responses.low: Talks too fast and makes jokes
stress_responses.medium: Goes very quiet and starts taking notes
stress_responses.high: Disappears for two days, then returns with a plan and a guilty expression

contradictions: Deeply believes in community autonomy but has already violated it in a way he hasn't fully reckoned with
habits: Leaves tiny data offerings at E.L.F. shrines wherever he goes — not from faith exactly but from respect
Keeps a physical fieldwork journal in addition to his neural recorder because he doesn't trust the glitchy implant
Cooks for people when he doesn't know how else to help
breaking_points: Incontrovertible proof that his work directly caused harm to a specific community
Being physically threatened is less breaking than being morally compromised

physical_description.heritage: West African / Scandinavian / Caucasian (Quliyev suggests Central Asian or Russian lineage)
physical_description.build: Lean and long-limbed, slight forward stoop from years hunched over fieldwork notes; wiry rather than athletic, the build of someone who walks everywhere and forgets to eat
physical_description.hair_style: Short, close-cropped, slightly unkempt; appears to be cut every six months out of necessity rather than intention
physical_description.eye_color: Modified: slow-rotating geometric pattern in amber and charcoal overlaying dark brown iris
physical_description.skin_tone: Dark reddish-brown with warm undertones; shows the wear of daily outdoor fieldwork across variable weather
physical_description.complexion: Angular face with pronounced cheekbones; close beard that grows patchy at the jawline and is visibly neglected (two-year maintenance gap evident); deep worry lines that deepen in direct light, making him appear significantly older than thirty-four; slight dark circles under eyes suggest chronic sleep deficit from note-taking and fieldwork
distinguishing_marks: Faint scar across left knuckle from a fieldwork incident (2219) — thin white line approximately 2cm long
Minor burn scar on right forearm (thermal exposure during infrastructure documentation) — pale, roughly circular, 1cm diameter
Worn groove on left ring finger from constant note-taking stylus use
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Modded irises with visible slow-rotating amber and charcoal geometric pattern — immediately noticeable during eye contact; pattern rotates in 12-second cycles. Neural recorder port barely visible at left temple (hairline-level, thin scar, minimal aesthetic intervention). No visible chrome or subdermal plating.
physical_description.posture_movement: Forward-leaning walk as if always listening; hands gesture while speaking but palms-up rather than dominant; habitually touches temple (neural recorder engagement); sits with knees drawn up even in formal contexts; eyes track foot traffic and social groupings even during conversation — occupational observation habit
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 3 working academic: three-outfit rotation of durable, mended cotton-blend layers (grays, dark blues, earth tones); one slightly better set for University Spine presentations (unfashionable, carefully maintained); worn hiking boots resoled twice; carries a canvas fieldwork satchel with visible stains from multiple neighborhoods; no corporate logos; clothes show authentic wear rather than styled distress; thermal undershirt visible at collar in cold months
